mcat_description.short: Prefabricated steel buildings are factory-fabricated structural steel systems — comprising primary frames, secondary members, and cladding — designed, detailed, and assembled on-site using bolted connections for industrial, commercial, and institutional use.
mcat_description.long: Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEBs) are integrated steel structural systems in which primary rigid portal frames (tapered built-up I-sections), secondary members (purlins, girts, eave struts), and roof/wall cladding are designed as a complete system, fabricated off-site under controlled factory conditions, and rapidly erected on-site. Structural design in India follows IS 800:2007 (general steel construction), IS 875 (wind and snow loads), IS 1893 (seismic design), and IS 2062 for structural steel grades (E250, E350). PEBs dominate industrial and warehousing construction in India due to large clear spans (typically 18–90 m), faster construction timelines (30–50% shorter than conventional), and lower foundation loads versus RCC. Buyers procure on a turnkey basis — covering design, fabrication, supply, and erection — with lead times of 8–12 weeks from order to delivery.

market_context: Prefabricated steel buildings in India are commercially dominated by the Pre-Engineered Building (PEB) system — factory-fabricated structural steel frames assembled on-site — which has become the preferred construction method for industrial warehouses, factory sheds, and logistics hubs across India. The Indian PEB market is governed by IS 800:2007 (general steel construction), IS 875 (wind/snow loads), IS 1893 (seismic design), and IS 2062 for structural steel grades (E250, E350 being most common); some manufacturers also design to AISC and MBMA codes for export or multinational clients. Major Indian PEB vendors include Tata BlueScope, Pennar Industries, Everest Industries, Zamil Steel, and Kirby India, with a large unorganised segment of regional fabricators. Clear spans of 18–36 m are typical for Indian industrial projects, with single-span capability up to 90–100 m for hangars and sports facilities. Buyers procure on a turnkey basis (design + fabrication + erection) with lead times of 8–12 weeks; crane-compatible PEB frames (up to 50-tonne overhead crane capacity) command a significant premium over standard frames. The market is growing, driven by India's logistics and warehousing boom, PLI scheme-linked manufacturing expansion, and MSME industrial shed demand.
